evals.name: quote-sanity-check
evals.prompt: We just got a quote of $4.20/unit for a Texas Instruments single-cell battery-management IC: 8-pin package, I2C interface, -40 to +85C industrial grade. Is that a fair price, and what's actually driving the cost? Use the P2Predict tool in this repo (the trained battery-management-IC model is in models/, named ridge_unit_price_at_1_usd_*.model). The CLI is .venv/bin/p2predict and .venv/bin/p2predict-train; repo root is /Users/ahmedhafsi/Dev/P2Predict.
evals.expected_output: A point prediction for the part, a likely-range interval (so the $4.20 quote can be judged fair/high/low against a defensible band, not a single number), and a per-feature SHAP attribution explaining the drivers. Should sign-check the attribution and caveat low-importance/under-sampled features rather than over-claiming.

evals.name: build-should-cost-model
evals.prompt: I have a CSV of about 100 battery-management ICs with specs and unit prices at case-studies/battery-management-ics/data/bmics_clean.csv (target column is unit_price_at_1_usd). Build me a should-cost model from it and tell me how good it is. Use the P2Predict tool in this repo: the CLI is .venv/bin/p2predict-train; repo root is /Users/ahmedhafsi/Dev/P2Predict.
evals.expected_output: Trains a model with p2predict-train. For a price target on a small dataset, should pass --log-target on (or at least reason about it) and avoid --feature-outliers drop. Should judge model quality by residual-bias (unbiasedness), not R2 alone, and ideally produce the PDF quality report via --report.

evals.name: supplier-switch-whatif
evals.prompt: We're sourcing a 16-cell EV/datacenter battery pack monitor currently from ADI/Maxim (48-pin, I2C, -40 to +125C automotive grade, multi-cell). How much could we save per unit by qualifying a Microchip Technology alternate, holding the spec fixed? Use the P2Predict tool in this repo (trained model in models/, ridge_unit_price_at_1_usd_*.model; CLI is .venv/bin/p2predict; repo root /Users/ahmedhafsi/Dev/P2Predict).
evals.expected_output: Uses a what-if comparison (--whatif swapping manufacturer to Microchip Technology) to return the per-unit delta and percentage, framed as a sourcing lever. Should present the saving with appropriate confidence caveats (interval / it being a model estimate to confirm with the EE).
